Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We're ready to proceed with a customer-led dry run next week but want to confirm a couple of specifics before we lock a window. Quick questions: 

- Primary goals: validate streaming concurrency behavior (open streams), stable p95 latency under streaming load, and max sustained throughput for our inference flows. Can you confirm how Redwood measures "open stream" concurrency vs. per-request concurrency?
- Target SLOs we discussed: p95 latency < 200ms for short-chat endpoints, sustained throughput target ~180 req/s across the suite, and ability to handle 220 concurrent open streams with graceful degradation. Are these realistic for the hardware profile we talked about (g4dn-like nodes + burst pool)?
- For the load driver we plan to use k6 (we have some Locust tests too). We'll want to run a smoke + ramp + sustained 30m hold. We can share our k6 scripts (attached v3) and test accounts.

Attachments: cobalt_k6_script_v3.js (text), cobalt_test_accounts.csv (csv)

Can you send an allowlist of IP ranges we should use and the preflight checklist so our infra team can lock a window? Looking at Wed 28th or Thu 29th — timezone PST.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of QA, Cobalt.ai

---
On Wed, Jul 20, 2027 at 11:30 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great sync earlier. I'm looping Marissa and Ethan for ops/streaming details.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: quick follow-up from today's perf sync — dry run ask

Alex — thanks for the note and the scripts. High level answers up front, then a concrete preflight checklist and proposed slots.

Short answers:
- Open-stream concurrency vs request concurrency: Redwood counts an "open stream" as an active long-lived connection (e.g., a streaming response where the client keeps the HTTP/2 or SSE channel open). Per-request concurrency counts each request/response cycle. For streaming SLOs we surface both: active_streams.p95 and request_latency.p95. We'll map your k6 flows to both metrics in the runbook.
- Preliminary feasibility: the numbers you cited are within an expected envelope for the config we discussed, but we'll want to validate with a customer-led rehearsal. Expect us to recommend a small policy tweak for KV cache sizing if you lean on many prefix-shared contexts.
- k6 vs Locust: either works. k6 gives more reproducible distributed ramps; Locust is fine for ad-hoc interactivity. We'll run from our dedicated load agents and allow you to run your external agents — both sets of IPs will need to be allowlisted.

Preflight checklist (action items):
1) IP allowlist: Redwood will provide the set of outbound IPs for our load fleet + ingestion endpoints by EOD tomorrow. You should provide your inbound agent IPs (yours and any third-party load generators).
2) Test accounts: confirm the CSV of test API keys; we'll create sandbox tenants and shadow keys.
3) SLO matrix: confirm endpoints you want measured (chat-short, chat-long, embed, rerank). We'll use p50/p95 and error-rate thresholds. Please review attached SLO matrix draft.
4) Window options: Thu Jul 29 09:00-12:00 PST (preferred) or Fri Jul 30 02:00-05:00 PST (alternate). Please confirm ASAP.
5) Observability hooks: provide a shared Datadog dashboard link or S3 log target for raw traces.

I'll attach the SLO doc we last used (slo-matrix.pdf) and the k6 stub that maps to our metrics. Marissa — can you confirm streaming limits and the KV-cache note? Ethan — can you advise on whether we need a temporary autoscale uplift for the burst window?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: quick follow-up from today's perf sync — dry run ask

Quick internal note copied to the thread so customer sees the timelines.

We validated the expected profile for the planned hardware. Summary:
- Sustained throughput: 180 req/s across chat endpoints (aggregate) looks fine for the ded. pool if we size to 6 x n1-standard equivalent nodes; recommend enabling burst pool for short ramps up to 260 req/s for up to 2 minutes.
- Streaming concurrency: we can support 220 concurrent open streams but recommend testing at 250 for a short spike to observe graceful degradation. We'll track active_streams.p95 and stream_close.error_rate.
- Latency: p95 request latency target of <200ms is achievable for short-chat when context sizes are <512 tokens. For longer contexts (>=1024 tokens) expect p95 to rise; include those in the script for a separate validation.
- Autoscale uplift: Ethan suggests a temporary +30% GPU reservation across the dedicated pool for the window to reduce risk of queueing.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: publish load fleet IPs and a CIDR list by EOD Tue 27th (attachment: allowlist-range.txt).
- Ethan: authorize +30% uplift for Thu 29 08:30-12:30 PST and create a rollback plan.
- Priyom: instrument the k6 script to emit custom tags for open_stream_id to ensure we capture stream lifecycles.

I'll drop the allowlist and timeline in the HubSpot deal and DM infra owners.

—Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
